$comment: Clause identity, content and the delta that armed a check. Licensing: clause.schema.json.license (REUSE sidecar).
title: MAINLINE console — clause version and delta witness
description: mainline.clause_version (ARCHITECTURE.md §5.3) plus the DeltaVerdict / DeltaWitness contract published by the algorithms domain (mainline_domain.contracts). Decision D8 there: a weaken/remove with delta_basis='lattice' whose witness rows were not written in the same transaction is REFUSED by fn_delta_witness_guard with P0001 — an unexplainable weaken verdict does not get to exist. When the witnesses are nonetheless absent from a payload, the console renders an explicit WITNESS UNAVAILABLE state and never an inferred explanation.

parent.description: The ancestor version this one edits, when the read API resolved it.

gen.description: Denormalised from commit_obj for bisect ordering.

activity_root.description: The level-1 archival activity code. It is also the vector-index prefix, which is why blame survives an asset-tag churn.

canon_text.description: Offsets are ALWAYS into canon_text. The console highlights spans against this string and no other.

anchor_set.description: Tags, setpoints, citations, CAS numbers, roles. An anchor dropped between versions is one of the residue reasons.

cat_json.description: The normalised Control Assertion Tuple. Shape is owned by the algorithms domain; the console renders it as structured data and asserts nothing about its internals.

blood_root.description: MMR root over the severity-monotone lineage accumulator (M2).

sev_max.description: The worst severity anywhere in this version's blame lineage. Projected; never chosen.

delta_witness.description: One element of the minimal unsatisfiable subset behind a delta verdict. Field names mirror mainline_domain.contracts.DeltaWitness exactly.

delta_verdict.description: mainline_domain.contracts.DeltaVerdict. `witnesses` may be null — meaning the payload carries no witness rows — which the console renders as WITNESS UNAVAILABLE. An empty array is a DIFFERENT claim: the emitter says there are none.

minimal.description: Whether the witness set is a minimal unsatisfiable subset. Null when the emitter did not establish minimality — an unproven claim of minimality is worse than none.
